points.title: Restoration Kingdoms
points.boundary_rationale: The supplied c. 2100–1900 BCE coordinate is retained because it captures several responses to third-millennium political change. Their strongest relevance is staggered: Ur III ends near the middle of the Point, Middle Kingdom Egypt begins within it, the first Cretan palaces belong at or just after its closing boundary, and Šimaški is most visible through the Ur III collapse and successor order.

points.title: Old Babylonian World
points.boundary_rationale: The supplied c. 1900–1600 BCE range is retained because it substantially matches the conventional Old Babylonian period and captures major contemporary systems around it. Assignment-level ranges expose the uneven fit: Babylon rises from one competing dynasty to regional dominance and ends near 1595 BCE; Middle Kingdom Egypt ends around 1650/1640; Cretan court-centered systems transform around 1700; and the richest Old Assyrian merchant archives belong principally before the end of the eighteenth century.

points.title: Great Bronze Age Powers
points.boundary_rationale: The supplied c. 1550–1200 BCE coordinate is retained as a staggered comparative window. New Kingdom Egypt begins near the opening but continues to c. 1070; Kassite rule emerges through an obscure transition and continues to c. 1155; the Hittite imperial phase enters around c. 1400 and ends near 1200/1180; Middle Assyrian expansion enters with Ashur-uballit I around 1365 and continues beyond the endpoint. The supplied terminal label therefore marks a regional transition corridor rather than a universal fall.

points.title: Early Iron Age
points.boundary_rationale: The supplied c. 1200–900 BCE coordinate is retained as a transition window rather than a synchronous four-state tableau. It begins amid continuing Egyptian, Kassite, Assyrian, coastal Levantine, and Anatolian-successor histories and ends at the threshold of better-attested ninth-century kingdoms and Neo-Assyrian expansion. Assignment-level relevance, source type, and later textual memory must carry the precision.

points.title: Kings, Prophets, and Assyrian Expansion
points.boundary_rationale: The supplied c. 900–722 BCE range is retained as a sequential Levantine–Assyrian interaction window. It begins when the Point I labels become better-attested kingdoms, city-states, and inscriptional communities. It ends with the supplied fall of Samaria, while Phoenician cities and Assyria continue and Aramaean polities are annexed unevenly. The exact attribution and sequence of Samaria's conquest and reorganization remain debated across Shalmaneser V, Sargon II, biblical, chronicle, and royal-inscription evidence.

points.title: Assyrian Apex
points.boundary_rationale: The supplied 722–612 BCE range is retained. Its opening follows Samaria's fall and Sargon II's accession; its closing is the supplied destruction of Nineveh. The endpoint is a major Assyrian capital and heartland collapse, not the final disappearance of Assyrian kingship: Ashur-uballit II continued from Harran until 609. Judah, Saite Egypt, and Nabopolassar's Babylon also continue beyond 612, so every assignment receives its own terminal or continuation note.

points.title: Neo-Babylonian World
points.boundary_rationale: The supplied 612–539 BCE range is retained. The opening is Nineveh's fall, although Assyrian resistance continues to 609 and Nabopolassar's dynasty began in 626. The closing is Cyrus's capture of Babylon and the end of the Neo-Babylonian dynasty. Judah's kingdom ends conventionally in 587/586, independent Median kingship around 550, and Saite rule only in 525; the Point therefore records four different transitions rather than one synchronized imperial block.

points.title: Achaemenid World
points.boundary_rationale: The supplied 539–336 BCE range is retained. Cyrus's capture of Babylon opens an Achaemenid-centered coordinate, although Saite Egypt remains independent until 525 and no single event in 539 creates the Greek or Macedonian assignments. The 336 endpoint marks Philip II's death and Alexander III's accession, not the Achaemenid Empire's fall: Darius III and the empire continue until Alexander's campaigns end Achaemenid kingship in 330. Egypt's 525, 404, and 343 transitions and Macedonia's late rise therefore require assignment-level phase labels.

points.title: Alexander and the Diadochi
points.boundary_rationale: The supplied 336–281 BCE range is retained. Alexander's accession opens the coordinate, but his Asian invasion begins in 334, Darius III dies and Achaemenid kingship ends in 330, Alexander dies in 323, Ptolemy receives Egypt in 323 and assumes kingship in 305/304, Seleucus's durable return to Babylonia dates to 312/311 and his kingship to 305/304, Ipsus repartitions power in 301, and Corupedium ends the Lysimachus–Seleucus contest in 281. The Point is therefore a sequence of formation thresholds rather than one stable Diadochi settlement.

points.title: Mature Hellenistic World
points.boundary_rationale: The supplied 281–146 BCE range is retained as a long phased coordinate. Antigonus II's durable Macedonian rule begins only in 277/276; the Antigonid monarchy ends at Pydna in 168 and Macedonia then passes through Roman reorganization and renewed war before 146. Greek poleis and koina remain active throughout and beyond the endpoint, although the Achaean War and Corinth's destruction transform their political environment. Ptolemaic rule continues to 30 and Seleucid rule to 63, with major internal and territorial transitions at Raphia, the Great Revolt, Magnesia and Apamea, and the mid-second-century dynastic conflicts. Assignment-level phases therefore override any impression of uniform stability or synchronized termination.

assignments.research_status: Reviewed long-phase dossier; archive geography, temple-state negotiation, labor and tax status, Great Revolt chronology, dynastic conflict, and 146 continuation require continuing audit; assignment remains Working.

assignments.research_status: Reviewed long-phase dossier; regional control, eastern losses, treaty terms, local agency, dynastic chronology, coercion, and post-146 continuity require continuing audit; assignment remains Working.

manifestations.name: Foundation Archive
manifestations.description: A distributed public record that joins every major structure to its authorship, materials, lawful scope, service dependencies, and maintenance history.
manifestations.canon_connection: Law of Identity; permanence; Presynce; Diamond and Hypergiant; Freemason; Proliteriate; Claim / Title / Yield; placement cue: Law of Identity, permanence, and Claim / Title / Yield
manifestations.possible_location: Working Stonebend placement associated with Law of Identity, permanence, and Claim / Title / Yield; exact siting requires geography review.
manifestations.possible_institution: existing Stonebend archive service
manifestations.hueman_hook: artifact provenance, building inspection, and maintenance-history references
manifestations.purpose: Keep the identity, authority, dependencies, materials, alterations, and maintenance obligations of every major Stonebend work publicly traceable.
manifestations.historical_ancestry: Sumerian administrative tablets and sealings, managed canal dependencies, and city-scale institutional organization.
manifestations.modern_house_interpretation: Stonebend converts early record practice into constitutional provenance: an archive supports Identity and maintenance but never grants Claim, Title, or Yield by itself.
manifestations.physical_appearance: A contemporary dark-blue civic interior with Stonebend materials, stepped reading levels, durable indexed surfaces, visible service diagrams, and foundation inscriptions; no literal ziggurat, cuneiform façade, or Mesopotamian costume.
manifestations.institutional_role: A documentation service inside existing Stonebend public-record and works authority, not a new office or court.
manifestations.gameplay_potential: Read-only building provenance, inspection context, repair history, archival research, and future restoration-quest hooks.
manifestations.implementation_notes: Reference `manifestation.stonebend.foundation_archive`; display source Gifts and current constitutional owner separately; require later runtime ownership before any state mutation.
manifestations.confidence: High for recordkeeping and urban institutions; medium for any single archive form across the full Point range.

manifestations.name: Territorial Stewardship Registry
manifestations.description: A public registry makes the scope, local custody, service dependencies, and reporting path of distributed Stonebend works legible without creating imperial power.
manifestations.canon_connection: Law of Identity; permanence; Presynce; Diamond and Hypergiant; Freemason; Proliteriate; Claim / Title / Yield; placement cue: Law of Identity, permanence, and Claim / Title / Yield

manifestations.possible_institution: existing Stonebend public-record and works authority
manifestations.hueman_hook: jurisdiction lookup, works provenance, service handoff, and maintenance context
manifestations.purpose: Make the delegated scope, local custodian, reporting path, service dependencies, and maintenance responsibility of distributed Stonebend works publicly traceable.
manifestations.historical_ancestry: Old Akkadian governors and local institutions, Akkadian and Sumerian scribal continuity, messenger reporting, and long-range administrative coordination.
manifestations.modern_house_interpretation: Stonebend translates layered territorial administration into bounded public stewardship; the registry identifies authority but cannot create Claim, Title, Yield, or central supremacy.
manifestations.physical_appearance: A contemporary dark-blue civic interface and records hall with layered jurisdiction maps, parallel-language records, service diagrams, change histories, and local custody markers; no palace, victory stele, or imperial insignia is copied.
manifestations.institutional_role: A documentation and coordination service within existing Stonebend public-record and works authority, not a governorate or new ministry.
manifestations.gameplay_potential: Read-only jurisdiction lookup, public-work provenance, maintenance dependencies, translated record comparison, and future repair or inspection context.
manifestations.implementation_notes: Keep current constitutional owner, historical source, and translation version as separate fields; never infer authority from geographic scale or an ancestral tag.
manifestations.confidence: High for layered administration, bilingual scribal practice, and reporting; medium for the uniformity of control across all claimed Akkadian territory.

manifestations.name: Civic Obligation Ledger
manifestations.description: A public maintenance ledger records measured obligations, deliveries, work dates, responsible offices, exceptions, and completion evidence without reviving ancient labor control.
manifestations.canon_connection: Law of Identity; permanence; Presynce; Diamond and Hypergiant; Freemason; Proliteriate; Claim / Title / Yield; placement cue: Law of Identity, permanence, and Claim / Title / Yield
manifestations.possible_location: Working Stonebend placement associated with Law of Identity, permanence, and Claim / Title / Yield; exact siting requires geography review.
manifestations.possible_institution: existing Stonebend works and records authority
manifestations.hueman_hook: maintenance schedule, delivery provenance, responsibility handoff, and exception review
manifestations.purpose: Make every measured civic obligation, delivery, work interval, responsible office, exception, and completion record inspectable across the life of a public work.
manifestations.historical_ancestry: Ur III administrative accounting, provincial delivery and redistribution archives, dated legal records, labor documentation, and year-name chronology.
manifestations.modern_house_interpretation: Stonebend receives accountable comparison, dating, custody, and maintenance responsibility. It rejects coerced labor, royal command, and the premise that an entry in a ledger creates constitutional authority.
manifestations.physical_appearance: A contemporary dark-blue records hall and distributed interface with Stonebend materials, calibrated surfaces, source-office marks, visible timelines, dependency maps, and amendment layers; no cuneiform wallpaper, royal statue, or copied ziggurat form.
manifestations.institutional_role: A record service inside existing Stonebend works, standards, and Title authority; it does not impose labor, assess tax, or create Claim, Title, or Yield.
manifestations.gameplay_potential: Read-only maintenance schedules, delivery provenance, work-history inspection, responsibility handoffs, exception review, and future bounded restoration context.
manifestations.implementation_notes: Keep ancient source type, archive, date formula, and coercion risk visible; separate historical accounting evidence from the modern office that owns a task.
manifestations.confidence: High for extensive administrative, dated, legal, and labor records; medium for treating the debated bala system as one uniform provincial mechanism.

manifestations.purpose: Let residents compare jurisprudence, contracts, measures, worked problems, source limits, and present authority in one inspectable civic-learning setting.
manifestations.historical_ancestry: Old Babylonian law collections, sealed legal and commercial records, scribal schools, sexagesimal place-value tables, and mathematical problem texts, with Babylon's changing political scope kept explicit.
manifestations.modern_house_interpretation: Stonebend receives public reasoning, documentation, units, worked procedure, and correction. It does not receive Hammurabi's kingship, unequal ancient penalties, coerced labor, or a second source of law, Claim, Title, or Yield.
manifestations.physical_appearance: A contemporary dark-blue civic interior with Stonebend materials, calibrated work surfaces, reversible case panels, contract and witness layers, source-object images, unit converters, worked diagrams, and visible corrections; no lawgiver throne, faux cuneiform wallpaper, or Babylon replica.
manifestations.institutional_role: A library, archive, and standards teaching program within existing Stonebend record, education, and Title boundaries; it cannot decide a case, certify a right, or promulgate law.
manifestations.gameplay_potential: Read-only case comparison, tablet provenance, unit and assumption inspection, curriculum references, translation history, error checking, and future bounded measurement or archive tasks.
manifestations.implementation_notes: Label the Hammurabi monument a royal law collection or jurisprudential monument rather than a modern code; show ancient social rank and coercion; attach provenience and genre to every contract and problem tablet.
manifestations.confidence: High for the law stele, contracts, sealed records, and mathematical problem tradition; medium for reconstructing any one standardized school curriculum across the full Old Babylonian world.
